Synergies. The FY2019 restructuring note set a $2,500M Celgene cost-synergy target with $2,800–3,000M of charges. The Q4 2020 call raised it to "approximately $3 billion by the end of '22" and reported $1.4bn achieved in 2020. No filing after 2021 reports realised synergies against either figure; the Q4 2022 call says only "over delivered synergies" with no number. Management stopped reporting against the target without ever confirming it landed.

The impairment register. $470M (2020, orva-cel), $840M (2021, Celgene haematology and fibrosis compounds), $98M (2022), $136M (2023), $2,900M (2024: $1,400M Augtyro, $590M alnuctamab, $390M a Celgene immunology compound, $280M Inrebic, $122M Abecma), $949M (2025: $564M Augtyro plus $385M across two oncology assets), and $830M in H1 2026 on an oncology asset and a radiopharmaceutical asset.

The divestiture record is worse than the acquisition record. BMS bought Amylin for roughly $7,000M including the assumed Lilly obligation in 2012, then sold the combined diabetes franchise eighteen months later for $2,700M upfront plus a royalty stream that has now stopped. That franchise generates roughly $8bn a year for AstraZeneca and BMS receives nothing from it. The final effect is a $1,121M pretax income headwind beginning in 2026 with nothing offsetting it, and the Q2 2026 10-Q confirms the mechanics with divestiture royalty income of $0 for the six months against $558M a year earlier. Note 4 states in every year that revenue and pretax earnings related to all divestitures "were not material," in the same note that discloses $1,121M of 2025 diabetes royalty income.

Two deals in the window worked. MyoKardia produced Camzyos, growing 73.9% in H1 2026 to an exit run-rate near $1.7bn against a $13,089M price, roughly 7.7x forward revenue. And the Celgene pipeline — not its marketed base — produced Reblozyl, Breyanzi, Zeposia and Abecma, $4,689M of 2025 revenue growing 30.7% further in H1 2026 on the three still separately disclosed. Those are the assets management said in January 2019 were the point of the transaction.

12. Capitalisation and balance sheet

BMS funds a $44.3 billion principal debt stack against roughly $14 billion of annual operating cash flow, with almost no near-term maturities, no financial covenants anywhere in the structure, and a principal-weighted coupon of 4.09%.▪ Net debt peaked at a year-end level of $38,470M at 31 December 2024 and has declined $6,814M in eighteen months to $31,656M at 30 June 2026, entirely out of operating cash flow because no stock has been repurchased since 2023. The exposures that matter are not on the debt schedule.

The stack. All 44 instruments are senior unsecured notes ranking equally with each other; none is secured, and there are no financial covenants on the notes or on the revolver. Grouped by maturity decade:

Bucket Principal $M % of stack Weighted-average coupon
2026–2030 8,851 20.0% 3.11%
2031–2035 9,277 20.9% 4.36%
2036–2040 4,752 10.7% 4.01%
2041–2045 5,205 11.7% 4.34%
2046–2050 7,772 17.5% 3.99%
2051–2055 6,599 14.9% 4.83%
2056 and later 1,867 4.2% 4.90%
Total principal 44,323 100% 4.09%

Weighted-average cost of debt = principal-weighted coupon across all instruments, 4.09%. The single $500M floating note at SOFR plus 0.49% moves the blend by less than a basis point and was repaid in H1 2026. Cross-check against realised expense: FY2025 interest expense of $1,891M over average principal of $46,630M is 4.06%, three basis points apart, so the coupon table is complete. Cash interest differs from book interest in both directions: FY2025 interest payments were $2.1bn against $1,891M of expense, and H1 2026 payments were $789M against $818M of expense, because a $751M unamortised purchase-price adjustment on the acquired Celgene debt reduces book interest while tender timing moves cash. The better forward estimate is the 4.09% coupon on $42,421M of current principal, about $1.74bn.

Weighted-average maturity is 15.9 years and eighty percent of principal is due after 2030, and the near-dated tranche has the lowest coupons. Aggregate maturities are $2.0bn (2026), $2.0bn (2027), $544M (2028), $2.2bn (2029) and $2.1bn (2030) — $8.9bn, 20% of the stack, over five years against $14,156M of FY2025 operating cash flow. There is no refinancing wall. The debt marks at 92.6% of carrying value at 31 December 2025 and 91.4% at 30 June 2026, implying a market yield roughly 55–70bp above the average coupon [estimate: price discount ÷ approximate modified duration of 12–13 years]; refinancing the $8.9bn due through 2030 at that level would add on the order of $50M of annual interest.

EUR-denominated principal is $6,550M, 14.8% of the stack, and roughly 86% of it is unswapped: the 1.750% 2035 euro note was reported at $598M at end-2024 and $676M at end-2025, a 13.0% increase from currency alone. And contractual floating exposure understates the real figure, because fixed-to-floating swaps designated as fair-value hedges had notional of $4,000M on the asset side and $555M on the liability side at 31 December 2025, so synthetic plus contractual floating exposure was $5,055M, 11.4% of principal, rather than the 1.1% the note schedule implies.

The 2025 liability-management trade. BMS Ireland Capital Funding issued €5.0bn in November 2025 for $5.7bn of net proceeds, fully and unconditionally guaranteed by the parent so there is no structural subordination, and BMS repurchased $8,739M of principal for $9,068M of cash through tenders and make-whole redemptions, recognising a $356M loss. Differencing the 2025 and 2024 principal columns identifies the retired paper exactly: a weighted-average coupon of 4.945%, about $432M of annual coupon, replaced by euro notes at 3.849%, about $226M. The trade retired about $200M of annual coupon and reduced principal $2.9bn net at a cash premium of $329M, a payback of about 1.6 years. Interest expense for H1 2026 was $818M against $979M a year earlier. It also moved a sixth of the stack into euros with almost no swap coverage.

The revolver is $5.0bn, extended in January 2026 to a January 2031 termination date, undrawn at all three dates, with no financial covenants. Commercial paper capacity was reduced from $7.0bn to $5.0bn in January 2025 and nothing was outstanding at either year end; the revolver backs the programme, so short-term ratings are the operative constraint on that line rather than revolver size. Moody's rates the company A2 with a stable outlook and S&P A with a stable outlook; S&P downgraded from A+ to A after the December 2023 acquisition announcements and affirmed the A rating with a stable outlook on 21 January 2026 [web]. Leases are immaterial at a $2,028M total liability, and pension is overfunded by $100M.

Leverage through the cycle. On EBITDA excluding acquired IPRD and impairments, net debt to EBITDA is 1.54x at LTM June 2026 against 1.70x for FY2025 and 1.97x for FY2024. The 12.14x FY2024 GAAP figure is an artifact of expensing $13,373M of acquired IPRD in one year. Leverage that year was 2.5x on EBITDA ex-IPRD. Depreciation and amortisation in the cash-flow statement fell 58%, from $9,600M (FY2024) to $4,011M (FY2025), as the Celgene-era intangibles finished amortising ($8,872M to $3,317M).

Share count and dilution. Diluted shares went from 1,637M (2018) to 2,258M (2020) on the Celgene issuance, an increase of 38%, and $28.3bn of buybacks between 2019 and 2023 took the count back only to 2,032M, still 24% above 2018. The count is now rising: 2,032M (FY2024), 2,039M (FY2025), 2,048M (Q2 2026 and H1 2026). Treasury shares are declining — 902M, 894M, 887M — because shares are issued out of treasury to settle compensation with nothing coming back in. Net issuance runs roughly 7–8M shares a year, about 0.4% annual dilution, the first sustained dilution since 2020. Stock-based compensation of $553M in FY2025 is 1.1% of revenue and is not an earnings-quality issue on its own; the issue is that nothing offsets it.

Accrued rebates and discounts moved more than debt did. They are in other current liabilities, and went from $9,021M (31 December 2024) to $8,844M (31 December 2025) to $5,654M (30 June 2026). The cash flow statement shows the matching outflow: a $3,135M use of cash in H1 2026 against a $254M source in H1 2025. Operating cash flow declined to $4,497M from $5,871M, down 23%, while earnings before income taxes rose 54% to $7,326M. Accrued rebates had been functioning as several billion dollars of interest-free financing; cutting the Eliquis list price shrinks the gross-to-net gap, so the accrual settles at a structurally lower level. The $3.2bn is a one-time payout and the float does not come back.

Obligations that are not on the balance sheet.

Obligation Amount Status
Contingent R&D milestones to third parties $18.3bn ($9.6bn pre-Phase-III, $8.7bn post-Phase-III) Payable only on achievement; not accrued
Sales-based milestones $21.5bn Payable only on achievement; not accrued
Celgene CVR litigation $6.4bn claimed Disputed, not accrued; three of five claims proceeding
BioNTech anniversary payments $2.0bn across 2026–2028 Payable unless BMS terminates the agreement
BioNTech and SystImmune contingent milestones up to $7.6bn each Contingent
Mirati contingent value right about $1.0bn face, recorded at $607M On balance sheet, fair-valued through earnings

The $18.3bn plus $21.5bn of milestones is $39.8bn, roughly 90% of the funded debt stack, and none of it is on the balance sheet.▪ Most of it is probability-weighted. A pharmaceutical balance sheet at 1.9x therefore comes with contingent obligations that an industrial balance sheet at 1.9x does not. The Mirati contingent value right is a liability that grows when the pipeline succeeds: it went from $256M to $607M in 2025 on revised assumptions about the probability of a regulatory milestone.

Structural risks, ranked.

  1. A fixed $44bn stack against an EBITDA base with disclosed exclusivity losses on three of its four largest lines. At LTM EBITDA of $16,816M and net debt of $31,656M leverage is 1.88x; hold the debt constant and cut EBITDA 40% and leverage goes to 3.1x with interest coverage from 7.9x to 4.0x. Neither breaches anything, because there is nothing to breach, but both would matter to the ratings, and the ratings determine access to the commercial-paper programme.
  2. The rebate-accrual drawdown, which makes FY2025 operating cash flow an overstatement of near-term available cash by roughly $3bn.
  3. The contingent claims above, $39.8bn of them.
  4. The unswapped euro exposure: $6,550M of euro principal, 86% of it unswapped.
  5. Refinancing cost, which is small and slow — on the order of $50M of added annual interest.

None of the usual credit worries applies: no covenants, no structural subordination, no secured layer, an undrawn $5.0bn revolver and a pension overfunded by $100M.

13.3 What actually drove the decade

Gross margin. Reported gross margin ran 69–79% across the decade with no trend, peaked at 78.6% in 2021 when Revlimid was at $12,821M, and settled at 71.1% in 2024–2025. Neither driver of the decline is operational efficiency. The first is that alliance profit sharing runs through cost of products sold — $6,980M to Pfizer and $7,181M to all partners in FY2025 against $14,443M of Eliquis revenue — so Eliquis's rising share of mix drags consolidated gross margin down. The second is intangible impairment charges booked to cost of products sold, $1,839M in 2024 falling to $564M in 2025.▪ BMS's reported gross margin is also not comparable to peers that load acquired-intangible amortisation into cost of goods: BMS states explicitly that it excludes it, and loading it back takes FY2023 from 76.2% to 56.1%, FY2024 from 71.1% to 52.7% and FY2025 from 71.1% to 64.2%. The 11.5-point improvement in that adjusted measure between 2024 and 2025 is the amortisation roll-off, not an operating improvement.

Operating margin. One deal inverts GAAP operating margin in 2020 and 2024, so the GAAP series has no trend. On the ex-IPRD-and-amortisation basis the series is 27.0% (2019), 30.7%, 40.0%, 40.5% (2022), 38.3%, 30.6% (2024), 35.4% (2025), 34.4% in Q2 2026. The peak was 2022. The 2024 trough was cost of products sold rising $3,275M on impairments and R&D rising $1,860M; the 2025 recovery was SG&A declining $1,147M on the strategic productivity initiative and R&D declining $1,208M. Underlying operating margin today is four to six points below the 2021–2022 peak and has not recovered to it.

Returns. Pre-Celgene BMS earned 23.6% ROIC (2017) and 39.9% (2018) on $10–14bn of invested capital; post-Celgene it has earned 9.0–15.5% on $52–82bn in the years GAAP operating income was positive, and negative returns in 2020 and 2024.

Working capital and capital intensity. Days inventory outstanding rose to 194 in 2019 on the Celgene inventory step-up and normalised to 64–91 thereafter. Days sales outstanding rose from 62 (2020) to 73 (2025); receivables grew 33% while revenue grew 13% over that window. Capex is structurally light at 1.8–2.7% of revenue post-Celgene against 4–6% pre-Celgene. The capital intensity is entirely in acquired intangibles rather than at the plant level.

Per-share outcomes. Revenue per diluted share went from $11.56 (2016) to $23.64 (2025), an 8.3% compound rate. Free cash flow per diluted share went from $1.10 to $6.30, still below the 2021 level of $6.79, with a decade high of $6.88 in 2024 despite $19,443M of buybacks over 2021–2023. Diluted shares are still 24.6% above the 2018 pre-Celgene level of 1,637M. Over the full decade BMS generated $110,140M of operating cash flow on the restated basis used in this section (§10.3 shows $108,663M as filed), and spent $10,669M on capex, $72,879M on acquisitions, $31,309M on buybacks and $38,173M on dividends.

Over twelve months consensus has revised FY2026 EPS up 14.9% and FY2027 up 13.0%, while FY2028 moved only 2.6%. Across the Q2 print it passed 74% of the 2026 revenue raise into 2027 and 28% into 2028.

Two things the street's own numbers do not internally reconcile. The consensus 2027 revenue line implies the Growth Portfolio decelerating from roughly +11% to about +5% with nothing inside it losing exclusivity, which either reflects a flat-to-down Opdivo franchise offset by eleven compounding brands, or a line built by taking 2026 up and holding the 2027 decline to the size of the guided Eliquis step-down.▪ And the consensus 2028 line applies a 40% decremental margin to a $6.2bn revenue decline, which is defensible only because roughly half of the lost Eliquis revenue takes its cost with it — the same mechanism the model in §17 relies on, so the two are not independent confirmation of each other.

Management guides revenue and other income low and beats it, guides operating expense low and overspends it every year, and gross margin and the tax rate come in close.▪ FY2025 is the cleanest full cycle: revenue guided at about $45.5bn and delivered $48,194M; gross margin guided at about 72% and delivered 72.6%; operating expense guided at about $16.0bn and delivered $16,641M; other income guided at about $30M and delivered $814M; the tax rate guided at about 18% and delivered 18.8%. The headline FY2025 EPS "miss" of $6.15 against a $6.40–6.60 October range is not an operating miss: guidance explicitly excludes acquired IPRD incurred after the guidance date, the October range assumed $(0.80) of IPRD impact and the year landed at $(1.40), so on the guided basis the year delivered $6.75, above the top of the range. The $0.60 delta is the Q4 Orbital Therapeutics charge, a capital-allocation decision.

Three mechanical points. FY2017's GAAP P/E of 101x reflects the $0.61 GAAP EPS produced by U.S. tax-reform charges. FY2023's perfect-foresight multiple of 44.6x is the same artifact seen one year early.

The Q2 2026 print shows how the market is now treating these beats. It was the largest combined beat in the series — +27.4% on EPS and +10.5% on revenue, with full-year guidance raised on both lines — and produced a same-day move of +2.8%, against +11.4% for the comparable +29.1% EPS beat in Q2 2024. On EPS alone the largest surprise in the series was Q2 2025 at +36.1%, which produced a −5.8% session. The Q2 2026 revenue beat is a channel-accounting effect: gross product sales declined 18% year over year while net product sales rose 6%, because the gross-to-net adjustment moved from 46% to 30% on the January Eliquis list-price reduction. The next two prints on the new gross-to-net basis would settle whether the discount is durable.

These multiples are based on consensus estimates as of the 2026-08-07 close of $64.72; enterprise value of $168,274M is market capitalisation of $132,204M plus net debt of $36,070M. Consensus already models the exclusivity step: revenue declines 3.2% in FY2027, 12.9% in FY2028 and 9.7% in FY2029, and adjusted EPS declines 4.7%, 14.0% and 10.1% across the same years. Dispersion is widest in the years where earnings decline: the standard deviation of the EPS estimate goes from 2.0% of the mean in FY2026 to 6.0% in FY2027, 9.7% in FY2028 and 14.3% in FY2029. The FY2030 adjusted EPS estimate of $5.093 is identical to FY2029's to three decimal places on the same estimate count, which is more likely a carry-forward than an independent estimate set, so it is not used. Bloomberg's stored FY2025A figures differ from BMS's reported $6.15 non-GAAP and $3.46 GAAP; the reported figures are the ones used in the ten-year table above.

BMS has not historically traded on book value, so the ten-year table includes no price-to-book column. Book value carries no information here: fiscal-year-end price over book value per share was 6.6x (2014), 8.0x, 6.0x, 8.5x, 6.0x, 2.8x (2019), 3.6x, 3.7x, 4.8x, 3.5x (2023), 6.9x (2024) and 5.9x (2025), against 5.9x currently. The 2019 drop is the Celgene purchase, which took other intangibles from $1,091M to $63,969M and book value per share from $8.64 to $23.16, and the 2023–2024 rise is those intangibles amortising away plus $13.4bn of acquired IPRD expensed against equity in one year. The series moves on deal accounting.

Gilead's and Merck's FY2026 P/E prints are not meaningful. Gilead's FY2026 BEst adjusted EPS is $(0.43) against $9.87 for FY2027. Merck's FY2026 BEst adjusted EPS of $2.76 against $9.54 for FY2027 produces the 47x FY2026 print, and Merck's FY2026 estimate has been revised down 43.5% in three months and 71.3% in a year. Both are the same phenomenon that made BMY's own FY2024 non-GAAP EPS $1.15 — charges inside the adjusted consensus — and they are why the GAAP columns are in the table. BMY's FY2026 estimate revisions are among the largest positive in the pharmaceutical set, +9.8% over three months and +15.0% over one year on FY2026 and +7.5% and +12.9% on FY2027; only Regeneron (+14.7% and +32.9%) and, on the one-year number, Eli Lilly (+21.2%) are larger.

17. Forward model summary

Operating model only: no discounting to a per-share value. Revenue is built from twenty-two product lines rather than from a growth rate, and every scenario difference is a named change to a named driver. The model is based on BMS's own non-GAAP presentation with a GAAP bridge alongside, because management guides on it, consensus reports on it, and building on GAAP alone would make the forecast unreadable when one deal inverts the year. The build reproduces FY2025 as filed: non-GAAP gross profit $35,000M less SG&A $7,149M less R&D $9,492M gives non-GAAP operating income of $18,359M, plus other income of $814M and less acquired IPRD of $3,721M, taxed at 18.8% over 2,039M shares, reproduces the reported $6.15.

Revenue peaks in 2026 at $50.3bn and does not return there inside the horizon, falling 31.0% to $34.7bn in 2035 with a trough plateau of $34.8–35.0bn across 2030–2031. The 2026 peak comes from price: roughly $3.1bn of Eliquis growth against a $2.1bn net revenue increase, and Eliquis converts to gross profit at about 49 cents on the dollar.▪

There are two exclusivity waves, not one. The first removes $28,405M of 2027 revenue by 2031: Eliquis U.S. in April 2028, Opdivo in December 2028, Orencia from 2028, Yervoy. The second runs 2031–2036: Reblozyl 2031, Breyanzi, Sotyktu and Zeposia 2033, Cobenfy 2033 if the pending patent-term restoration grants, Opdualag 2034, Camzyos 2036. Those seven lines are $6,961M of FY2025 revenue and $15,940M of the model's 2030 revenue, 45.6% of that year.▪ It is why the mild 2032–2033 stabilisation reverses into a 2034–2035 decline rather than a recovery.

Margin holds up better than revenue for a contractual reason. Non-GAAP operating margin declines only 5.5 points from 38.1% (2025) to 32.6% (2030) against a 27% revenue decline, because 50.9 cents of every Eliquis dollar is cost of products sold. A dollar of lost Eliquis revenue costs about $0.49 of gross profit; a dollar of lost Opdivo revenue costs about $0.81.▪ Gross margin therefore rises to 76.5% in 2029 as Eliquis exits and then declines below the 2026 level by 2035, because the replacement wave arrives on partner economics.

The dividend stops being covered by free cash flow in 2029. With no buybacks, 2% dividend growth and $2bn a year of business development, net debt bottoms at $24.3bn in 2028 and re-levers to $35.3bn and 3.8x EBITDA by 2035, funded by paying an uncovered dividend.▪ Nothing in that path requires a failure. There are no financial covenants to breach, so the constraint is the ratings.

Ten-year revenue CAGR from FY2025: bear −8.3%/yr, base −3.2%/yr, bull +0.8%/yr. Cumulative 2026–2035 free cash flow is $16.4bn / $51.9bn / $106.4bn against cumulative dividends of $23.4bn / $53.2bn / $51.8bn. The bear is a fully stacked case, six independent drivers at roughly their twentieth-percentile outcome at once, so its joint probability is far below any single driver's; treat it as the shape of the downside rather than as a 20% likelihood. In the bear, management overspends against a falling top line for two years, then cuts operating expense 47% between 2027 and 2035, cuts the dividend in 2029 and eliminates it by 2032, and still lets net debt rise to $41bn on 7.6x EBITDA. The bull does not require a margin BMS has never earned: non-GAAP operating margin peaks at 41.8% in 2029 because a bigger launch portfolio is modelled as costing more to sell.

Eliquis is 30% of revenue and the whole of the sell-side debate on 2027. By 2032 and 2035 it is the smallest of the six sensitivities, because its revenue and 50.9% of its cost leave together. Its 2028 timing moves near-term cash flow materially, by $761M of 2029 operating income and roughly $3.2bn of cumulative 2027–2029 free cash flow, and it does not move where the company ends up. Two further single-line sensitivities are disclosed and dated rather than estimated: the royalty terminations remove $1,756M of near-100%-margin pretax income across two years, worth about $0.25 of 2027 EPS on its own, and the accrued-rebate unwind takes $3.0bn out of 2026 operating cash flow and $0.3bn out of 2027.

17.4 Assumptions and their source

Twenty-six assumptions have bear, base and bull values. Eighteen have weak evidence and are marked below.

Assumption Base Source Flagged weak, and why
Eliquis U.S. net revenue 2027 vs 2026 +2.0% management guidance Yes. The bear tests price, not exclusivity. Pfizer discloses a path in which generics could enter on 21 November 2026 if the formulation patent is invalidated on appeal, which would take 2027 U.S. Eliquis from $13.6bn to roughly $3–4bn — a $10bn swing against a bear that moves $1.9bn. The range should be widened to include that tail
Eliquis ex-U.S. 2027 vs 2026 −48.2% base rate Holds. An independent build gives −51.3%, inside the modelled range
Eliquis U.S. retained in 2028 41.2% of 2027 base rate Yes. BMS's own closest precedent is Plavix, which retained 36.1% of U.S. sales in a year with 4.5 months at brand price; re-applying that shape to a 1 April 2028 date gives about 26%, below the modelled bear of 36.8%. Pomalyst's first full generic quarter (−78%) and Sprycel's first full year (38.3% retained) bracket the base. The evidence supports a base nearer 32–35%; a ten-point shift is about $1.4bn of 2028 revenue
Pfizer profit share plus supply cost 50.9% of Eliquis revenue, held flat historical record Holds. Twelve years of disclosure across a nineteen-fold revenue increase, and it survived the 2026 reset
Opdivo franchise 2026–2028 CAGR +1.4%/yr historical record Holds. Base is already conservative against realised: FY2025 +12.1%, Q2 2026 +6.0%, and the 2026 figure requires H2 to turn slightly negative
Opdivo franchise retained in 2032 vs 2028 20.6% base rate Holds. A bottom-up geographic blend gives 19.8%; the U.S., EU and Japan dates lag each other, which no single-market precedent captures
Post-2030 core 2025–2030 CAGR 20.8%/yr historical record Yes, and this is the model's largest sensitivity. The base is a five-way joint success requiring Reblozyl +59% off a book already deep into its label, Camzyos to triple against aficamten, Cobenfy 17x, Sotyktu 3.8x from a product whose U.S. revenue declined in 2025, and Breyanzi 2.3x against apheresis capacity. Applying BMS's own realised 64%-of-plan delivery rate against the 2021 Investor Day gives a 15.8% CAGR, only 1.5 points above the bear. The base belongs nearer 16–18%
Cobenfy peak inside the horizon $3,100M our judgment Yes. The class ceiling is Vraylar near $3.0bn after eight years and Nuplazid, the closest analogue, near $560M; the mechanism has failed twice in public (AbbVie's emraclidine and Cobenfy's own ARISE); and the bear of $1,020M is 4x the current run-rate, so it is not an ADEPT-failure case. Evidence supports a base nearer $1.5–2.0bn
Orencia retained in 2030 vs 2027 33.8% historical record Yes. The 2027 denominator has Orencia growing to $3,850M, which assumes no IV biosimilar in the first plausible entry year; Dr. Reddy's BLA was accepted on 20 February 2026 with U.S. IV approval expected at end-2026 [web], worth roughly $400–500M of 2027 revenue
Near-term launch cohort 2032 $4,600M base rate Yes. The range is mechanical (bear exactly 60% of base, bull exactly 140%) against a documented 71% average deviation from one-year-pre-launch consensus, and admilparant and RYZ101 both have named competitive or physical constraints
Milvexian BMS-booked revenue 2032 $3,000M consensus Yes. The base is the success case labelled as the central one. The only prior Phase III of an oral Factor XIa inhibitor in atrial fibrillation, Bayer's asundexian, was stopped early for inferior efficacy against apixaban, and BMS's own sibling trial LIBREXIA-ACS was discontinued in 2025. Whether BMS books the revenue at all under an equal J&J profit share is unresolved; if it takes only a profit share the 2032 revenue line is $3.0bn too high
Pipeline wave 2, 2035 $7,500M base rate Yes. The 2021 analogue cohort that reached about $7.4bn in five years contained products already approved or filed; wave 2 contains one Phase III asset, one Phase I/II ADC, a preclinical in-vivo CAR-T and unnamed future business development. The line is a placeholder rather than a forecast of specific molecules, and it is 21.6% of 2035 base revenue
Legacy ex-Eliquis FY2026 $3,490M historical record Yes. It requires H2 of $1,409M against an H1 actual of $2,081M, a 32% sequential-half decline, while U.S. Revlimid rose sequentially from $348M to $425M in the two quarters after the caps lapsed. The base belongs at the top of its range
Non-GAAP gross margin FY2026 70.0% management guidance Yes on the range rather than the level. The 50bp band is narrower than the single observed guidance error, and H1 2026 is running at 70.8%, so the base requires H2 at about 69.2%, a 160bp sequential-half decline that the range does not test
Non-GAAP gross margin 2035 68.5% our judgment Yes. The scenario spread is produced by two undisclosed plugs (stranded overhead and an owned-Growth cost ratio) rather than by the partner-mix logic the justification describes. The underlying finding — that the replacement generation is lower-margin because of contracts already signed — is grounded
Stranded enterprise overhead by 2030 $800M historical record Yes. The cited evidence is on a GAAP basis and, decomposed, points the other way; on the model's own non-GAAP basis the 2025 variance implies a larger stranded block than assumed
Non-GAAP opex FY2026 $16,800M management guidance Yes on the range. A 1.8% band on a line whose GAAP-to-non-GAAP bridge cannot be resolved from the disclosure, in a year that includes the iberdomide launch. Extend the bear to about $17.4bn
Non-GAAP opex 2032 $15,000M our judgment Yes. The base cuts selling cost 12% while roughly doubling the number of products to sell, and the bear exceeds the precedents it cites
Other income and expense FY2027 $1,200M of net expense historical record Yes on the range. A ±7.5% band on the most volatile line in the P&L, which moved $1,514M in a single year, and one cited offset (the Winrevair royalty) is booked in revenue, not in this line
Effective tax rate 19.0% steady state management guidance Holds. The 17.5–20.0% range spans both directions of the mix argument and is above the OECD Pillar Two floor; one point on 2032 pretax income is about $0.05 of EPS
Acquired IPRD / BD expense from 2027 $2,000M/yr historical record Yes. The whole range is below the realised record: the ten-year mean is $3,251M/yr and the five-year mean $3,996M/yr, and cumulative 2027–2035 spend of $13.1–19.2bn is below any of them run-rated forward. The range should include at least one mega-deal-sized year
Diluted share count 2032 2,099M historical record Yes. Zero buybacks for ten years is a policy assumption, not a base rate, against $28.3bn repurchased between 2019 and 2023 and $9.7bn of modelled surplus free cash flow across 2026–2028; and the range is asymmetric, with the base at one end of it
Dividends paid 2030 $5,450M historical record Yes. Dividing modelled dollars by modelled shares gives dividend per share peaking in 2029 and then declining below the 2026 level, so the base embeds a per-share reduction while the narrative reserves the cut for the bear; and it funds a cumulative 2029–2035 shortfall of $10,968M with debt
Capital expenditure, 2026–2035 average $1,330M/yr historical record Yes. The modelled path declines 14% from 2027 to 2030–31 while the justification says capex holds; capex-to-depreciation breaks the band it is calibrated against; and the disclosed U.S. onshoring commitments are absent
Working-capital cash effect FY2026 −$3,000M historical record Yes on the range. H1 2026 alone shows a $(3,135)M rebate outflow, so the base implies H2 nets to +$135M, on a line that may still be falling
Operating cash-flow conversion 93%, identical in all scenarios historical record Yes. The stated calibration does not reproduce against FY2025 without an unexplained working-capital term, and simple conversion by year has ranged 64% to 113%. Holding it constant is deliberate — it makes scenario cash-flow differences attributable to operating drivers — but it should decline in the outer years

The model reproduces FY2026 guidance before departing from it ($6.88 at the midpoint against a guided $6.75–7.00), and its cost build reconciles to FY2025 as filed with the owned-Growth cost ratio falling out as a residual within 40bp of an independent bottom-up build.

Four projected years show operating income moving against revenue, and none of them is operating leverage in the usual sense:

  • 2026. A 3.1% incremental margin: Eliquis converts at 49 cents on an opex line that rises $159M.
  • 2028–2030. Decrementals of 41–74%, the same mechanism in reverse, with the mix of what is being lost shifting from Eliquis to Opdivo and Orencia.
  • 2031–2035. Operating income declines on flat revenue because partnered assets at 42–50% partner cost substitute for wholly owned ones at 19%, the arithmetic consequence of deal structures BMS has already signed.

Where the base departs from consensus: +1.0% on 2026 revenue and +2.5% on 2026 EPS, +3.0% and +3.1% on 2027, and −2.4% on 2028 EPS. The 2027 gap is the one that matters: the base models +9.5% against consensus's implied +5% (§14). Confidence declines materially after 2031, and from 2032 the pipeline-wave-2 line is sized from reinvestment productivity rather than from named assets.

18. Risks

R1 — The 2028 exclusivity cliff on 65% of revenue. Five products lose exclusivity inside a twenty-six-month window: Eliquis ($14,443M, U.S. 2028 under settlements, EU November 2026, Japan 2026), Opdivo ($10,049M, U.S. 2028, EU 2030, Japan 2031), Orencia ($3,705M, no U.S. date disclosed), Yervoy ($2,900M, no U.S. date disclosed, EU 2026) and Opdivo Qvantig ($238M, U.S. 2028). On retained economics the exposure is roughly $24bn, about 50% of revenue. BMS's own base rate for what follows: Revlimid peaked at $12,821M in 2021, was $2,951M in FY2025 and is running at about $1.7bn annualised, −87% from peak; Pomalyst went from $3,545M (FY2024) to $816M annualised within one quarter of U.S. generic entry.▪ Leading indicators: whether any Opdivo Qvantig formulation patent issues; the number of paragraph-IV notice letters disclosed each quarter (seven arrived for Camzyos in a single quarter); Orencia U.S. revenue after a Dr. Reddy's IV biosimilar approval; and ex-U.S. Eliquis revenue from Q4 2026.

R2 — Government-set prices on three of the four largest lines, with no legal remedy left. Eliquis from 1 January 2026, Pomalyst from 1 January 2027, Orencia selected in January 2026 for prices from 2028. The FY2025 10-K adds two new hooks: products may be selected on "potentially expanded future criteria," and maximum fair prices "could be renegotiated." The constitutional challenge failed at every level through certiorari denial in May 2026. U.S. Eliquis plus U.S. Orencia is roughly 27% of revenue now under or scheduled for administrative pricing. The Pomalyst exposure is small: U.S. revenue was already down to $131M in Q2 2026 before the price applies. Leading indicator: the HHS selection list published each January. A fifth-year list naming Opdivo, Reblozyl or Camzyos would be the escalation.

R3 — Both replacement assets slipped in the same quarter, and neither delay was a data event. Milvexian's atrial-fibrillation readout moved from late 2026 to Q1 2027 on the pace of events; the Cobenfy ADEPT programme moved to "early 2027 and be spread across the year" on enrolment pace and slower relapse accrual. Cobenfy is $155M of FY2025 revenue against a Karuna acquisition charged $12,122M to acquired IPRD, so all of the value ascribed to Karuna is in these readouts; milvexian has no revenue and $277M of BMS R&D payments to J&J in 2025. Countervailing evidence: delays in event-driven superiority studies are ambiguous and the independent data monitoring committee continues to endorse the study. Against that, an analyst asked on the same call about "a number of Phase III setbacks in recent years" and whether BMS had "actively addressed study conduct deficiencies," and the Chief Medical Officer attributed Phase III failures partly to trial execution.

R4 — $1,756M of near-100%-margin royalty income disappears across 2026–2027. The AstraZeneca diabetes royalty of $1,121M is already out of the 2026 base; Keytruda ($588M) and Tecentriq ($47M) leave on 1 January 2027, the same year as the guided Eliquis step-down. That is 18.8% of FY2025 pretax income with no cost to remove alongside it. The Merck Winrevair royalty is growing, from $107M in 2024 to $289M in 2025, and replaces a fraction of the loss. Leading indicator: the Other (income)/expense note each quarter.

R5 — Goodwill and intangibles of 175% of equity, with impairments running. At 30 June 2026 goodwill of $21,740M plus other intangibles of $17,387M totals $39,127M against total equity of $22,319M. In-process R&D of $6,770M is unamortised and tested for impairment, and $830M of it was written off in H1 2026 alone, 11% of the opening balance, on "a partial write-down of an oncology asset based on recent clinical results" and "a partial write-down of a radiopharmaceutical asset driven by an indication realignment." The FY2025 risk factor now concedes that impairments happen "as we have done in the past." Leading indicators: the IPRD balance quarter to quarter; any failed Phase III among the pumitamig pivotals, RYZ101's ACTION-1 or the CELMoD programmes; and the Mirati contingent value right, fair-valued through earnings at $607M.

R6 — The 2026 Eliquis optics reverse in 2027. Guided 2026 growth of 20–25% implies about $17.5bn, and management guides a $1.5–2.0bn step-down in 2027 attributed on the Q4 2025 call to the EU patent expiry and "rapid and steep decline like we have seen with other small molecules outside of the U.S." Non-U.S. Eliquis was $4,205M in FY2025, so the guided step-down requires 36–48% of the entire ex-U.S. base to disappear in one year with no U.S. give-back at all. An analyst put the objection on the record twice and did not get a U.S.-specific answer. Leading indicators: international Eliquis revenue in Q4 2026 and Q1 2027; whether the $1.5–2.0bn range is reaffirmed when 2027 guidance is issued.

R7 — A claimed $6.4bn contingent-value-rights obligation that survived dismissal. The successor trustee alleges BMS breached the Celgene CVR agreement by failing to use "diligent efforts" to obtain FDA approval of liso-cel before a contractual milestone date, "thereby allegedly avoiding a $6.4 billion potential obligation." In December 2025 the court found the plaintiff to be the successor trustee and allowed three of five claims to proceed. No trial date is set and no accrual is disclosed. $6.4bn is 91% of FY2025 net earnings and about 5% of market capitalisation. It is the one risk uncorrelated with the operating calendar, so it can arrive in a year when nothing else is going wrong. Other live matters: Thalomid and Revlimid antitrust opt-out suits, the Pomalyst antitrust class action on appeal, a Plavix Texas qui tam action, and an Arkansas 340B action filed in July 2026.

R8 — U.S. channel economics and an expanding 340B fight. U.S. gross-to-net reached 53% of U.S. gross product sales in FY2025 from 49% in FY2024. BMS's attempt to move 340B to a cash-rebate model was rejected by HRSA and it lost at the district court in May 2025, with the D.C. Circuit hearing argument in November 2025; the Arkansas Attorney General sued in July 2026 over contract-pharmacy conditioning. The FY2025 risk factor adds that BMS cannot "procure data sufficient to identify duplicate claims" associated with rising 340B utilisation. Mentions of 340B inside Item 1A went from one in FY2018 to fourteen in FY2025, a larger relative escalation than the IRA. Each percentage point of U.S. gross-to-net is roughly $710M of net revenue [estimate: 1% of FY2025 U.S. gross product sales derived from the disclosed rate].

R9 — Three wholesalers route about 90% of U.S. gross sales and all three agreements expire in June 2027. McKesson 36%, Cencora 29% and Cardinal Health 22% of FY2025 U.S. gross revenues, and the Q2 2026 10-Q puts the three at "approximately 90% of total gross sales of U.S. products during the six months ended June 30, 2026." BMS renegotiates the fee on 90% of U.S. gross sales at once, and no party discloses the rate.

R10 — The U.S. Government Agreement is a terminable shield against a live tariff. The Q2 2026 10-Q discloses tariffs on "patented pharmaceuticals and associated pharmaceutical ingredients" imposed by a Presidential Proclamation dated 2 April 2026. BMS is exempt until January 2029 under the December 2025 agreement and is not subject to future U.S. pricing mandates "while the agreement remains in effect. However, such exemptions may be terminated or may not be extended." BMS names the products dependent on third-party API and drug substance but never names a supplier or a country of origin, and gives no split of cost of products sold by manufacturing location.

R11 — PD-1/VEGF substitution, on management's own criterion. The class threatens $11,472M of FY2025 revenue. BMS's own stated test, from the CEO in June 2025, is that "the vast majority of the value that will accrue in this class is going to go to those agents that are either in the first or second position," and ivonescimab is ahead. BMS's stated strategy for pumitamig is "replace and expand. We want to replace PD-1, PD-L1 inhibitors," so if the class works it erodes Opdivo before 2028 regardless of who wins. Committed: $1.5bn upfront expensed in 2025, $2.0bn of anniversary payments that are contractual rather than contingent, up to $7.6bn of milestones, and a 50/50 profit share.

R12 — Cell-therapy and radiopharmaceutical manufacturing. CAR-T requires an unbroken chain of identity and custody, and "even slight deviations at any point in the production process… could result in loss of product or regulatory remedial action." New in FY2025: radiopharmaceutical third-party suppliers "may still be developing appropriate processes, controls, technologies and facilities, particularly for large-scale production," and the products "have time-limited stability once manufactured." Since FY2024 the CAR-T class also has a boxed warning for T-cell malignancies. Revenue exposed is $1,785M, 3.7% of FY2025. Leading indicators: any FDA Form 483 or warning letter at Devens, Bothell, Summit, Leiden or Indianapolis; a Breyanzi supply interruption in the product commentary; the ACTION-1 readout.

How these arrive together. Seven of the twelve are scheduled events inside a 26-month window rather than open-ended risks.

The bad case is the calendar running as disclosed while the two replacement assets fail to arrive.▪ In that case R1, R2, R3, R4 and R6 arrive together, and R5 follows mechanically because a milvexian or ADEPT failure would trigger impairment against a $6,770M in-process R&D balance. Cash generation is not yet impaired: $14,156M of operating cash flow in FY2025 against $5,045M of dividends and $1,311M of capex leaves roughly $8bn a year of discretionary cash to meet those events. BMS's historical response to a shock has been a large acquisition, which is what feeds R5.

One thing improved in 2026 that the risk factors do not reflect. The FY2025 10-K states that Eliquis generics "have entered the market in Finland, Poland and Portugal"; the Q2 2026 10-Q states they have entered in Poland only, with Portugal and Greece upheld positive on appeal, Denmark now positive, and Croatia and Hungary settled positive. The incorporated risk factor still names three generic markets where the Q2 2026 10-Q names one. Against that, the Q2 2026 Part II Item 1A says there have been "no material changes" from the FY2025 risk factors, while Part I of the same filing discloses an April 2026 agreement permitting a U.S. Orencia IV biosimilar on approval against a product with no disclosed exclusivity date and $3,705M of revenue, seven paragraph-IV filings against Camzyos, and a live tariff from which BMS is exempt only by a terminable agreement.

19. Source disclosure

Primary sources. Ten Forms 10-K (FY2016–FY2025), six Forms 10-Q (2024-Q3 through 2026-Q2), 43 earnings calls (Q4 2015 to Q2 2026), 133 presentation transcripts (2016 to June 2026), and 18 investor-presentation PDFs with 786 rendered slides (June 2020 to July 2026). SEC XBRL companyfacts for BMY and for eleven peers were pulled 2026-08-08. Every price, total-return, consensus and comparable-company series is from a live Bloomberg terminal. CMS Medicare Part D, Part B and NADAC datasets were queried directly on 2026-08-08, as was the openFDA Drugs@FDA API for ANDA and NDA approval counts by active ingredient. Peer filings for MRK, PFE, ABBV, JNJ, LLY, AMGN, GILD, REGN, AZN, NVS, MCK, COR, CAH and BNTX were read alongside. The 2024, 2025 and 2026 DEF 14A proxy statements and 115 Form 4 filings were read from EDGAR.

Basis of the constructed financials. BMS reports no operating income line; the consolidated statements of earnings run from total revenues straight to total expenses to earnings before income taxes. Every operating-income figure in §13 is therefore constructed as total revenues less cost of products sold, SG&A, R&D, acquired IPRD and amortisation of acquired intangibles, with the adjusted line excluding the last two, and each year is shown on the latest 10-K's basis. Non-GAAP diluted EPS is the exception, shown as originally published, because that is the number guidance was measured against. Core operating margin excludes acquired IPRD and intangible amortisation so the series is comparable across years and peers.

Gaps and failures.

  • Guidance ranges are disclosed only in the Form 8-K earnings releases. The FY2021–FY2024 non-GAAP operating-margin path and FY2020 worldwide Revlimid and Pomalyst revenue live only there; where a guidance figure below is sourced to a transcript rather than a filed table, that is why. FY2020 worldwide Revlimid and Pomalyst revenue is not recoverable, so the "low double-digit revenue CAGR excluding Revlimid and Pomalyst, 2020–2025" target cannot be scored.
  • No sell-side notes. The numeric consensus is solid (Bloomberg, weekly, four months of history plus twelve-month revision columns). The narrative consensus — each house's thesis, the estimate behind it, the bear case at full strength — comes from press summaries and from the analyst questions on the calls, which are a primary record of what covering analysts are arguing about but a narrower source than the notes themselves.
  • Risk-factor history. The deltas in §18 come from Item 1A of the ten 10-Ks, diffed at sentence level.
  • No consensus dispersion beyond FY2026. Bloomberg returns null for the high and low estimate fields on this terminal, and free aggregators put 2027 and later behind a paywall. Standard deviation and estimate counts are populated and are used for the ±1 s.d. bands. No consensus of any kind exists beyond CY2028; the only 2029–2030 figure recoverable is an expert's recollection of about $35bn, which pre-dates the 2026 guidance raise.
  • No unit, volume, prescription, patient-count, market-share or persistency metric exists in any BMS filing for any product in any period. Every unit figure in §1 is derived, and the duration-of-therapy assumption is the dominant sensitivity. No IQVIA or Symphony prescription series was available by any route, which is the one thing that would settle the 2026 Eliquis price-versus-volume split.
  • No franchise profitability exists. One GAAP segment, consolidated net income as the CODM measure, and a three-way R&D split as the only segment expense disclosure. Every product or portfolio margin here is a construction.
  • Bloomberg method note. Sampling a relative forward-period override inside a historical request does not return the consensus for the quarter being reported at each historical date. Every quarterly consensus figure in §15 uses that quarter's own absolute period code, sampled on the last session before the release.
  • External datasets. Both available external datasets (openFDA approvals and clinicaltrials.gov trial starts) are described in Appendix C and are marked not yet pulled.

Discrepancy log, summarised. Ten source disagreements were logged and eight were resolved. Four material ones: the Daloopa extract reported FY2018–FY2020 revenues of $5,973M / $7,945M / $11,068M against the filings' $22,561M / $26,145M / $42,518M and was rejected on period attribution; the standard XBRL amortisation tag is populated from the rounded narrative footnote rather than the statement line and is wrong by $150–500M a year; FY2021 non-GAAP EPS is $7.51 as published and $7.16 as restated under the 2022 definition change, and the as-published figure is used because it is what guidance was measured against; and a secondary FY2025 Legacy ex-Eliquis decline of 37% is 40.8% on the filings, which is used here. Two disagreements are recorded rather than resolved: the Ono royalty implied by the disclosed 4%/15% rates on disclosed product revenue is roughly $0.8–1.1bn, while the alliance-payments table leaves only $201M for every non-Pfizer partner combined, and BMS never discloses the amount; and BMS and Pfizer disclose materially different exclusivity pictures for the same asset, with Pfizer naming a 2031 formulation patent, an April 2028 date and a November 2026 downside that BMS's own table does not show.

Web sources. Roughly 55 external pages across about 35 domains, with the heaviest use of company investor-relations and results pages (bms.com, merck.com, jnj.com, abbvie.com, amgen.com, gilead.com, roche.com, astrazeneca.com, cytokinetics.com, summittxinc.com), regulator and government data (data.cms.gov, aspe.hhs.gov, api.fda.gov, cms.gov), industry analysis (drugchannels.net, iqvia.com), and financial aggregators (stockanalysis.com, marketbeat.com, tipranks.com). Full entries with access dates and supporting passages are in Appendix B.

Claims flagged [web, unverified]. Three, each because the underlying page could not be re-fetched: the FDA's own statement that generic prices decline more than 95% below the pre-generic brand price with six or more competitors (fda.gov returned 404 on direct fetch; the figures reproduce consistently across indexed renderings); the Citeline/Biomedtracker phase-transition and likelihood-of-approval rates used as an industry base rate; and the study finding that actual peak sales diverge from one-year-pre-launch consensus by an average of 71% with roughly two-thirds of launches missing expectations. All three are used as directional base rates and none supports a conclusion on its own.

20. What we still don't know, and the monitoring set

Unresolved gaps that bear on a section's conclusion.

  1. BMS attaches no economics to its pipeline. It names more than 45 assets by phase with dated PDUFA dates, and the 2023 R&D Day set per-programme probability-of-success targets, but no asset carries a disclosed population, probability or revenue. The "pipeline wave 2" block in §17 is 21.6% of 2035 base revenue and is sized from reinvestment productivity rather than from named assets, so the terminal revenue and every post-2031 scenario spread attach to no named molecule — the largest gap here.
  2. Ex-U.S. revenue of $13,828M, 28.7% of the total, is disclosed only in aggregate. BMS gives no Europe, Japan and rest-of-world split and no country-level revenue, so the November 2026 EU Eliquis expiry cannot be sized against the $4,205M ex-U.S. line and the UK NHS branded-spend cap, EU health-technology assessment and Japanese off-cycle price cuts cannot be quantified. Roughly a third of the checkpoint franchise is behind EU 2030 and Japan 2031 dates, which is what sets the trough year in §17.
  3. BMS publishes no measure of R&D productivity. R&D was $9,951M in FY2025, 20.6% of revenue and larger than the entire Legacy Portfolio excluding Eliquis, and there is no cost-per-approval, attrition-by-vintage or cycle-time disclosure to set against it. Whether $12.5bn a year of R&D plus business development can produce a replacement portfolio is answered here only by an industry-wide base rate marked low confidence.
  4. BMS does not disclose where it manufactures what. Item 2 names eight significant manufacturing sites and the euro debt is issued from an Irish entity, but no product, cost or country-of-origin split is given, so the tariff exposure in R10 carries no number one year before the tariff relief expires.
  5. What management did through BMS's last cliff, 2011–2016, is not established. The financial series here starts in FY2016 and all five key inflections fall in August 2016 or later, so that cliff appears only in fragments: a revenue trough in §6 ($21,244M in 2011 to $15,879M in 2014, with the peak regained only in 2018), a Plavix U.S. retention rate in §17.4, and single rows for the AstraZeneca diabetes divestiture in §9 and §11. It is the one full observation of this company behaving through a cliff.
  6. Consensus stops at CY2028 and no estimate dispersion is published beyond FY2026, so §14's three-way comparison has no external column across 2029–2031, precisely the recovery years where the internal, external and base-rate views disagree most.
  7. The gross-to-net reserve rollforward is disclosed only annually. The 10-K gives it by category, which is the one filed series that separates the revenue effect of the January 2026 list-price cut from the cash effect, and it is not available quarter by quarter across that boundary. It is the largest near-term uncertainty in both the capitalisation and the model.
  8. No party discloses what the wholesaler distribution service agreements pay. McKesson, Cencora and Cardinal route about 90% of U.S. gross revenue and all three agreements expire in June 2027. §5's finding that wholesalers are not extracting the spread comes from their segment margins, not from a fee disclosure.
  9. Whether 65% of revenue losing exclusivity in a twenty-six-month window is a company fact or a sector moment is unresolved. IQVIA sizes industry brand losses at nearly $200bn through 2030, but that total is not broken out against each named peer's own share, year and molecule.
  10. BMS's investor-presentation record runs June 2020 to July 2026 rather than a full decade, with nothing between the November 2021 Investor Day and the January 2023 JPM deck and nothing between the December 2023 Karuna deck and the January 2025 JPM deck, so the Appendix A gallery covers 2020–2026 only.

Specific open questions.

  • Has any Opdivo Qvantig formulation patent been granted, as opposed to applied for? This determines whether $3.3–4.4bn of converted revenue survives 2028.
  • How much of the 2026 Eliquis growth is volume and how much is the gross-to-net reset? An apixaban prescription series would settle it and would materially tighten the 2027 assumption, which is the widest bear-to-bull spread in the near years.
  • What is the 2027 Eliquis base management is actually working to, now that the 2026 base has risen by roughly $1.4bn and the step-down range has not moved?
  • Does BMS book milvexian revenue, and at what share? The J&J collaboration is described as equal global development-cost and profit sharing, but which party is principal for revenue recognition is not restated in current filings.
  • What is the dollar amount of Ono royalties in cost of products sold, and where in the disclosure do they appear? Without it the Growth Portfolio gross margin cannot be tightened below the 80–84% band.
  • What royalty does BMS pay Halozyme on Opdivo Qvantig? The product management is relying on to extend the largest franchise past 2028 has an undisclosed third-party claim on it.
  • Where does the accrued-rebate balance settle after the Eliquis list-price reduction fully works through? It went from $8,844M to $5,654M in six months and may still be falling; a $1bn lower settling point costs about $1bn of 2027 operating cash flow.
  • What does management intend for the dividend once free cash flow stops covering it? No leverage target and no payout policy is disclosed, and the $5.0bn repurchase authorisation has been untouched for eleven quarters.
  • Is there a fifth-year IRA selection risk on Reblozyl, Camzyos or Opdivo? The FY2025 10-K notes selection criteria "could be potentially expanded," and none of the three is in any scenario.
  • What do the wholesaler distribution service agreements pay, and what changes at the June 2027 simultaneous expiry?
  • Is there any accrual for the Celgene contingent-value-rights litigation? None is disclosed, and the general contingency language does not distinguish the $6.4bn claim.
  • What triggered the Chief Medical Officer change in mid-2025, three months after he bought stock on the open market? Neither the proxy nor any transcript explains it.

Appendix A — Investor-presentation insights and key slides

The decks give six years of dated, quantified targets; the 10-K gives no forward guidance at all. Set against realised results, they are a track record on management's own numbers.

  • A management target scorecard the filings do not contain (§8, §14). Investor Day 2021 slides 11, 124–127 set seven numeric commitments, scored one by one against realised results in §8. The revenue-CAGR target was met and everything about the composition of that revenue was missed [deck: Investor Day 2021, 2021-11-16, slides 11, 12, 124, 126].
  • Per-product 2029/2030 targets, and where each product actually is (§4). JPM 2023 slide 14 assigned $4bn-plus to each of Camzyos, Opdualag, Sotyktu and Reblozyl, $3bn-plus to Breyanzi and Zeposia, and $1bn-plus to Abecma. Their combined FY2025 revenue was $7,233M and their Q2 2026 annualised total is $8,572M. Two of the seven, Sotyktu and Zeposia, jointly targeted at more than $7bn, are running at a combined $868M with promotional support withdrawn in their largest indications. The target itself escalated before it was missed: about $20bn in the second half of the decade (June 2020) to $20–25bn in 2029 (July 2021) to $25bn-plus in 2029 (November 2021) to $25bn-plus in 2030 (January 2023) [deck: JPM 2023, 2023-01-09, slide 14].
  • Four of seven named 2029 revenue assets no longer exist (§2). Investor Day 2021 slide 120 named seven assets each promised more than $1bn of 2029 revenue. Bempegaldesleukin, the BCMA T-cell engager alnuctamab, cendakimab and MORAb-202 are absent from the January 2026 pipeline. Of the three survivors, milvexian's Phase 3 studies are run by Johnson & Johnson. Attrition beyond that headline list is broader still: more than twenty named programmes in the 2021 or 2023 pipeline charts appear in none of the 2026 ones [deck: Investor Day 2021, 2021-11-16, slide 120].
  • Business development was always meant to supply half the decade (§10, §11). JPM 2023 slide 27 states that business development would supply about 50% of expected 2030 revenue, off roughly 100 early-stage deals in 2019–2022. JPM 2025 slide 16 sizes the spend: about $28bn of R&D and about $27bn of business development in the three years to 30 September 2024, $55bn against a company generating roughly $46bn of annual revenue [deck: JPM 2023, 2023-01-09, slide 27; JPM 2025, 2025-01-13, slide 16].
  • A $4bn target retired in a footnote (§4). Q4 2025 deck slide 11, footnote 1: "Sotyktu is no longer promoted in dermatology in the U.S. and in a number of ex-U.S. markets." Psoriasis was the entire basis of the $4bn-plus 2029 target. Neither the JPM 2025 nor the JPM 2026 deck retracts the number; it simply stops appearing [deck: Q4 2025 results, 2026-02-05, slide 11].
  • The only product share series BMS has ever published (§4). Q2 2021 slide 9, sourced to Symphony Health: U.S. Eliquis total-prescription share 49% to 55% and new-to-brand share 59% to 63% between Q2 2020 and Q2 2021, with warfarin declining four points. BMS has not repeated a share chart for Eliquis in any later deck; from Q2 2023 the language reverts to unquantified market-share gains [deck: Q2 2021 results, 2021-07-28, slide 9].
  • The only launch funnel BMS has published for any product (§1). JPM 2023 slide 11 gives Camzyos REMS-certified physicians (more than 2,000 at 30 September 2022, more than 2,600 at 31 December 2022), patients in the hub (more than 1,100, then more than 1,800) and patients on commercial drug (more than 350, then more than 900), with about 70,000 symptomatic obstructive HCM patients in the U.S., a 20–25% diagnosis rate and potential to roughly double [deck: JPM 2023, 2023-01-09, slide 11].
  • A leverage commitment made three times with the date moved twice (§10, §12). Under 1.5x debt to EBITDA by 2023 (June 2020), by end-2024 (October 2020), then replaced in January 2025 by a $10bn debt-repayment target measured against the 31 March 2024 balance, which was a peak BMS created itself weeks earlier by debt-funding Karuna, RayzeBio and Mirati [deck: Investor Series, 2020-06-22, slide 4; MyoKardia, 2020-10-05, slide 19; JPM 2025, 2025-01-13, slide 16].
  • The buyback stopping, visible two ways (§10). JPM 2025 slide 16 reports about $16bn of share repurchases over the trailing three years; JPM 2026 slide 9 reports about $8bn over the trailing three years. A trailing figure that halves means the newest year contained none. The "about $5bn share repurchase authorization remaining" line is stated verbatim and unchanged at 30 June 2025, 31 December 2025, 31 March 2026 and 30 June 2026 [deck: JPM 2026, 2026-01-12, slide 9].
  • Ten points of non-GAAP gross margin in five years (§13). Guided at about 80% for FY2021, 72.6% actual for FY2025, guided 69–70% for FY2026 [deck: Q2 2021 results, 2021-07-28, slide 17; Q4 2025 results, 2026-02-05, slide 13].
  • Three R&D productivity targets never reported against (§2). R&D Day 2023 slide 12 set about ten INDs a year, a first-in-human-to-approval success rate of about 20%, and a median 6.5 years from first-in-human to approval; slide 134 added moving from six to twelve registrational assets within eighteen months; no subsequent deck scores any of the four [deck: R&D Day 2023, 2023-09-14, slides 12, 134].
  • The immunology retreat (§4). Q2 2025 slide 5 announces an immunology company formed with Bain Capital holding five assets, described as "selectively externalizing assets to maximize value creation," in the same quarter as the $1.5bn BioNTech alliance. Combined with Sotyktu's de-promotion and Zeposia's retreat to multiple sclerosis only, BMS has exited most of what it told investors in 2021 immunology would be [deck: Q2 2025 results, 2025-07-31, slide 5].
  • The market-sizing slides stopped when the dollar targets started being missed (§4). Investor Day 2021 slide 14 is the only bottom-up market map in the deck record, with dollar pools by tumour and indication. Every deck since substitutes patient counts for market dollars: JPM 2026 slide 5 sizes its five lead assets at about 10M, 15M, 700K, 3.5M and more than 200K patients with no revenue pool attached [deck: Investor Day 2021, 2021-11-16, slide 14; JPM 2026, 2026-01-12, slide 5].
  • Framing narrowed each cycle (§8). "Sustained top-quartile growth" (Karuna deck, December 2023) to "sustained top-tier growth by end of the decade" (JPM 2025) to "industry-leading sustainable growth into the 2030s and beyond" (JPM 2026). The adjective got softer and the horizon moved out.
  • The Opdivo inventory-build footnote (§6). Q2 2026 slide 9, footnote 2, discloses roughly $200M of sequential inventory build inside a reported Opdivo line of $2,485M and −3% year over year [deck: Q2 2026 results, 2026-07-30, slide 9].

Two gaps: nothing between the November 2021 Investor Day and the January 2023 JPM deck — the whole of 2022, when bempegaldesleukin failed — and nothing between the December 2023 Karuna deck and the January 2025 JPM deck, which itself refers back to a January 2024 communication that is not in the archive.

Appendix C — External data sources

Two external datasets are available, each marked not yet pulled (available on demand).

openFDA drug approvals (openfda_approvals). A free API over the FDA's Drugs@FDA database, keyed to the company's sponsor name as the FDA stores it, which is often a bare token rather than the legal entity name. It measures drug application approvals and submissions by sponsor over time, giving an annual approvals-by-year series. Source: https://api.fda.gov/drug/drugsfda.json. Cadence: as filed.

What it would inform here. First, §6 and §17: an independent, externally measured count of BMS's approval throughput against the standing commitment of "more than 10 new medicines and over 30 meaningful launch opportunities by 2030," which is currently the only quantified multi-year commitment management makes and which cannot be checked against any disclosed series. Second, §2: the record against the 2023 R&D Day productivity targets — about ten INDs a year, a 20% first-in-human-to-approval rate and a 6.5-year median cycle time — none of which BMS has reported against in three years. Third, §4.6: approved-ANDA counts by molecule for lenalidomide, pomalidomide, dasatinib and nab-paclitaxel, which is the source of the supplier-count column in the genericised-molecule table. Fourth, §13's operational-KPI subsection, where approvals per year would be the closest available proxy for the R&D productivity BMS does not disclose. Status: not yet pulled (available on demand).

clinicaltrials.gov trial starts (clinicaltrials_starts). A free API over the U.S. clinical-trials registry, keyed to the lead-sponsor name as clinicaltrials.gov spells it. It measures trial starts by phase and sponsor over time, giving an annual trial-starts-by-year series. Source: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies. Cadence: as filed.

What it would inform here. First, §6: whether the pipeline is being fed or drained, measured independently of the pipeline slides. The deck record shows more than twenty named programmes present in the 2021 or 2023 charts and absent from the 2026 one, and a trial-start series by phase would put a rate on that attrition rather than a list. Second, §4: the same series for Merck, AstraZeneca, AbbVie and the cell-therapy competitors would show whether BMS's registrational activity is keeping pace with the players taking share. Third, §17.4: the two model assumptions judged weakest — the post-2030 core compounding rate and the pipeline wave-2 block, which is 21.6% of 2035 base revenue and is currently sized from reinvestment productivity rather than from named assets — both depend on an assumption about how much clinical activity $12.5bn a year of R&D and business development actually buys. A Phase III start count by year is the closest external measure of that. Status: not yet pulled (available on demand).

Neither covers the two quantities named in §20 — an apixaban prescription series and product-level gross-to-net.
